subject: English
stem:
Match List I with List II:

| List I | List II |
|---|---|
| 1. Abysmal | A. Praise; tribute |
| 2. Encomium | B. Extremely bad |
| 3. Emulate | C. Imitate to equal or surpass |
| 4. Imbecile | D. Stupid or idiotic person |
solution: Abysmal means extremely bad, giving B. An encomium is a formal expression of high praise, giving A. To emulate is to imitate with the aim of equalling or surpassing, giving C. An imbecile is a stupid person, giving D. The complete matching is 1-B, 2-A, 3-C, 4-D. Matches option B.

subject: English
stem:
Match List I with List II:

| List I | List II |
|---|---|
| 1. Entice | A. Extremely idealistic; impractical |
| 2. Quixotic | B. Attract or lure |
| 3. Masticate | C. Chew |
| 4. Finicky | D. Hard to please; fussy |
solution: To entice is to attract or lure, giving B. Quixotic means impractically idealistic, giving A. To masticate is to chew, giving C. Finicky means fussy or hard to please, giving D. The complete matching is 1-B, 2-A, 3-C, 4-D. Matches option D.

subject: English
stem:
Match List I with List II:

| List I | List II |
|---|---|
| 1. Ignominy | A. Blame or burden of responsibility |
| 2. Paradox | B. Deep disgrace or shame |
| 3. Onus | C. Quandary or mire |
| 4. Insipid | D. Lacking flavour or excitement |
solution: Ignominy is public disgrace or shame, giving B. Onus is the burden of responsibility, giving A. Insipid means lacking flavour or interest, giving D. That leaves paradox with C by elimination. The complete matching is 1-B, 2-C, 3-A, 4-D. Matches option A.
reviewNote: Definition C, 'quandary or mire', is a poor gloss for 'paradox' (which properly means a self-contradictory statement). The pairing is forced by elimination; the other three are unambiguous.

subject: English
stem:
Match List I with List II:

| List I | List II |
|---|---|
| 1. Niggard | A. Very small amount or scarcity |
| 2. Pillory | B. Publicly criticize or ridicule |
| 3. Paucity | C. Mean or stingy person |
| 4. Sinister | D. Suggesting evil or harm |
solution: A niggard is a stingy person, giving C. To pillory is to hold up to public ridicule, giving B. Paucity is scarcity or a very small amount, giving A. Sinister means suggesting evil or harm, giving D. The complete matching is 1-C, 2-B, 3-A, 4-D. Matches option B.

subject: English
stem:
Match List I with List II:

| List I | List II |
|---|---|
| 1. Fervent | A. Lacking firmness; weak or limp |
| 2. Chagrined | B. Intensely passionate or enthusiastic |
| 3. Obeisance | C. Deep respect or deferential gesture |
| 4. Flaccid | D. Embarrassed or distressed |
solution: Fervent means intensely passionate, giving B. Chagrined means embarrassed or vexed, giving D. Obeisance is a gesture of deep respect, giving C. Flaccid means limp and lacking firmness, giving A. The complete matching is 1-B, 2-D, 3-C, 4-A. Matches option C.

subject: English
stem:
Match List I with List II:

| List I | List II |
|---|---|
| 1. Nonplussed | A. Confused or puzzled |
| 2. Clamour | B. Loud and continuous noise |
| 3. Prosaic | C. Dull or unimaginative |
| 4. Licentious | D. Morally unrestrained or depraved |
solution: Nonplussed means bewildered, giving A. Clamour is a loud continuous noise, giving B. Prosaic means dull and commonplace, giving C. Licentious means morally unrestrained, giving D. The matching is the straight order 1-A, 2-B, 3-C, 4-D. Matches option D.

subject: English
stem:
Match List I with List II:

| List I | List II |
|---|---|
| 1. Oaf | A. Persuade by flattery or deception |
| 2. Behemoth | B. Easily irritated or annoyed |
| 3. Peevish | C. Huge and powerful creature or entity |
| 4. Inveigle | D. Clumsy or unintelligent person |
solution: An oaf is a clumsy, stupid person, giving D. A behemoth is something enormous and powerful, giving C. Peevish means easily irritated, giving B. To inveigle is to win over by flattery or deceit, giving A. The complete matching is 1-D, 2-C, 3-B, 4-A. Matches option B.

subject: English
stem:
Match List I with List II:

| List I | List II |
|---|---|
| 1. Perfidy | A. Small or limited quantity |
| 2. Chastise | B. To scold or punish |
| 3. Apocryphal | C. Of doubtful authenticity |
| 4. Modicum | D. Betrayal or deliberate disloyalty |
solution: Perfidy is deliberate betrayal of trust, giving D. To chastise is to scold or punish, giving B. Apocryphal means of doubtful authenticity, giving C. A modicum is a small quantity, giving A. The complete matching is 1-D, 2-B, 3-C, 4-A. Matches option C.

subject: English
stem: Improve the underlined part: We'll have to \(\underline{\text{call off}}\) the experiment if the reagents don't arrive in time.
solution: 'Call off' means to cancel, which is exactly what the context requires when the reagents fail to arrive. 'Call on' means to visit or to request someone to speak, 'call up' means to telephone or to summon for service, and 'call in' means to summon someone for help. None fits, so the original is already correct. Matches option D.

subject: English
stem: Improve the underlined part: She was burning the candle \(\underline{\text{on both ends}}\) to meet the project deadline.
solution: The fixed idiom is 'burn the candle at both ends', meaning to exhaust oneself by working from early morning to late night. The preposition must be 'at', not 'on'. Option A changes the noun as well, and option B is ungrammatical because 'either' takes a singular noun. Matches option C.

subject: English
stem: Improve the underlined part: You can't \(\underline{\text{have the cake and eat it too}}\) in real life.
optA: eat the cake and have it too
optB: have your cake and eat it too
optC: have the cake or eat it too
solution: The standard form of the idiom is 'have your cake and eat it too', with the possessive 'your'. Option C's 'or' destroys the sense, since the point of the idiom is that the two cannot both be had. Matches option B.
reviewNote: Option A, 'eat the cake and have it too', is the logically stricter original form of this idiom and some keys prefer it. Keyed B as the standard modern usage.

subject: English
stem: Improve the underlined part: They were told \(\underline{\text{to not enter}}\) the restricted zone.
solution: A negative infinitive places 'not' before 'to', giving 'not to enter'. The printed 'to not enter' splits the infinitive. Option B needlessly makes it continuous and option C is ungrammatical. Matches option A.

subject: English
stem: Improve the underlined part: She sang so beautifully that even the critics couldn't \(\underline{\text{help but praised her}}\).
solution: The construction 'cannot help but' is followed by the bare infinitive, so it must be 'praise', not 'praised'. The modal 'could' already carries the tense, which also rules out option B's 'helped'. Option C changes the conjunction and keeps the wrong verb form. Matches option A.

subject: Physics
stem: An artificial satellite orbiting around the Earth does not fall down. This is so because the attraction of Earth
optA: does not exist at such distance
optB: is neutralized by the attraction of the Moon
optC: provides the necessary speed for its steady motion
optD: provides the necessary acceleration for its motion
solution: Gravity certainly acts on the satellite, so option A is wrong, and the Moon's pull is far too small and wrongly directed to cancel it, ruling out option B. The satellite's speed is set by the launch vehicle, not supplied by gravity, so option C misstates the role of the attraction. What the Earth's pull actually supplies is the centripetal acceleration that continuously turns the velocity vector, keeping the satellite on a curved path instead of a straight one. Matches option D.

subject: Physics
stem: A particle starts from rest and moves with uniform acceleration along a straight line. The percentage increase in displacement during the seventh second compared to that in the sixth second is about—
solution: For a body starting from rest, the displacement in the \(n\)th second is \(s_n = \frac{a}{2}(2n-1)\). For the sixth second \(s_6 = \frac{a}{2}(11)\) and for the seventh \(s_7 = \frac{a}{2}(13)\). The fractional increase is \(\frac{13-11}{11} = \frac{2}{11} = 0.1818\), that is 18.18 per cent. Matches option B.

subject: Physics
stem: A car starting from rest moves with uniform acceleration and attains a speed of 36 km/h in 5 minutes. What is its acceleration?
solution: The options are in km/h\(^2\), so work in those units. Five minutes is \(\frac{5}{60} = \frac{1}{12}\) hour. Starting from rest, \(a = \frac{v-u}{t} = \frac{36 - 0}{1/12} = 36 \times 12 = 432\) km/h\(^2\). Matches option B.

subject: Physics
stem: A passenger in a moving train tosses a five rupee coin. If the coin falls behind him, then the train must be moving with a uniform—
solution: While in the air the coin keeps the horizontal velocity the train had at the instant of the toss. If the train travelled a greater horizontal distance than the coin during the flight, the coin lands behind the passenger, which requires the train to have gained speed. That is uniform acceleration. Under constant speed or constant velocity the coin would return to the passenger's hand, and under deceleration it would land ahead of him. Matches option A.

subject: Physics
stem: A person of mass 60 kg is standing in a lift. If the lift moves downward with an acceleration of 2 m/s\(^2\), then the apparent weight of the person will be closest to—
solution: For a lift accelerating downward the normal reaction, which is the apparent weight, is \(N = m(g - a)\). Taking \(g = 10\) m/s\(^2\), \(N = 60(10 - 2) = 60 \times 8 = 480\) N. Using \(g = 9.8\) instead gives 468 N, which is still closest to 480 N. Matches option C.

subject: Physics
stem: The universal gravitational constant depends upon—
solution: In \(F = G\frac{m_1 m_2}{r^2}\) the masses and the separation appear explicitly and are therefore not part of \(G\). \(G\) is a universal constant: unlike the electrostatic constant it does not change with the intervening medium, and it has the same value everywhere in the universe. Matches option D.

subject: Physics
stem: A ball is thrown vertically upwards with an initial speed of 80 m/s. After hitting the ground, it loses 50% of its speed. What height will the ball reach after its first bounce? (\(g = 10\) m/s\(^2\))
solution: By symmetry the ball returns to the ground with the same speed it was thrown with, 80 m/s. Losing half of that leaves a rebound speed of 40 m/s. The height reached is \(h = \frac{v^2}{2g} = \frac{40^2}{2 \times 10} = \frac{1600}{20} = 80\) m. Matches option C.

subject: Physics
stem: Weight of a body on the surface of the Earth is \(W_1\). The weight of the same body is \(W_2\) at a height of 500 m above the surface, and \(W_3\) at a depth of 500 m below the surface of the Earth. Which one of the following is the correct relation?
solution: Gravity is strongest at the surface and falls off both above and below it, so \(W_1\) is the largest. For a small height, \(g_h = g\left(1 - \frac{2h}{R}\right)\), while for a small depth, \(g_d = g\left(1 - \frac{d}{R}\right)\). For the same 500 m the fractional loss above the surface is twice the loss below it, so the weight at height is the smallest of the three. Hence \(W_1 > W_3 > W_2\). Matches option C.

subject: Physics
stem: A device which is used in our TV set, Computer, Radio set for storing the electric charge is—
solution: A capacitor stores charge on its plates and energy in the electric field between them. A resistor dissipates energy as heat, an inductor stores energy in a magnetic field rather than as stored charge, and a conductor simply provides a path for current. Matches option D.

subject: Physics
stem: Let an electric current of 20 A flow through a conductor. What is the amount of charge that flows through it in 5 ms?
solution: Charge is current multiplied by time, \(Q = It\). Converting 5 ms to \(5 \times 10^{-3}\) s gives \(Q = 20 \times 5 \times 10^{-3} = 0.1\) C. Matches option A.

subject: Physics
stem: Vehicles transporting petrol or other inflammable substances are fitted with chains or metallic strips that drag on the ground. What is the main purpose of this arrangement?
optA: To reduce the friction between tyres and road
optB: To discharge static electric charge accumulated during motion
optC: To improve the stability of the vehicle
optD: To protect the vehicle from lightning
solution: Friction between the tyres and the road, and between the liquid and the tank walls, builds up static charge on the vehicle. If allowed to accumulate it could produce a spark and ignite the inflammable cargo. The trailing chain provides a conducting path so the charge leaks continuously to the earth. Matches option B.

subject: Physics
stem: An electric circuit consists of a cell, an ammeter and a uniform resistance wire. If the length of the wire is doubled, the ammeter reading—
solution: Resistance is proportional to length, \(R = \rho\frac{l}{A}\), so doubling the length doubles the resistance. With the cell's emf unchanged, Ohm's law \(I = \frac{V}{R}\) gives a current that falls to half its original value. Matches option B.

subject: Physics
stem: What happens during a short circuit in a household circuit?
optC: excess current flows which may cause heating
solution: A short circuit connects the live and neutral wires through a very small resistance. By Ohm's law the current becomes very large, and since the heat produced is \(I^2Rt\), that surge causes dangerous heating and can start a fire. This is precisely what a fuse or a miniature circuit breaker is installed to interrupt. Matches option C.

subject: Physics
stem: Two pieces of conductor of the same material and equal length are connected in series with a cell. One of the two pieces has cross-sectional area double that of the other. Which one of the following statements is correct?
optA: The thicker one will allow stronger current to pass through it
optB: The thinner one will allow stronger current to pass through it
optC: Same amount of electric current would pass through both the pieces, producing more heat in the thicker one
optD: Same amount of electric current would pass through both the pieces, producing more heat in the thinner one
solution: In a series connection the same current passes through every element, which rules out options A and B. Since \(R = \rho\frac{l}{A}\) and the lengths and material are the same, the piece with the smaller area has the larger resistance. Heat produced is \(I^2Rt\) with \(I\) common, so the thinner piece, having greater resistance, produces more heat. Matches option D.

subject: Physics
stem: In the circuit shown, a cell of 10 V is connected across two resistors \(R_1 = 1\ \Omega\) and \(R_2 = 2\ \Omega\) joined in parallel with each other. Find the current \(I\) drawn from the cell.
solution: For two resistors in parallel the equivalent resistance is \(R = \frac{R_1 R_2}{R_1 + R_2} = \frac{1 \times 2}{1+2} = \frac{2}{3}\ \Omega\). The current drawn from the cell is \(I = \frac{V}{R} = \frac{10}{2/3} = 15\) A. As a check, the branch currents are \(\frac{10}{1} = 10\) A and \(\frac{10}{2} = 5\) A, which sum to 15 A. Matches option C.
reviewNote: Figure-dependent: the printed question is a circuit diagram with the label 'Find the current'. The topology (10 V across 1 ohm parallel with 2 ohm, current I in the main branch) has been written into the stem, since the bank has no figure slot on this pipeline.

subject: Physics
stem: A copper wire of length \(l\) and cross-sectional area \(A\) carries a current \(I\). The power dissipated in the wire is \(P\). If an aluminium wire of the same dimensions carries the same current, the power dissipated will be—
solution: The power dissipated is \(P = I^2R = I^2\rho\frac{l}{A}\). With the current and the dimensions held fixed, the power is directly proportional to the resistivity. Aluminium has a higher resistivity than copper, which is why copper is preferred for wiring, so the aluminium wire dissipates more power. Matches option C.

subject: Physics
stem: A cell is connected across two parallel branches. One branch contains a bulb alone; the other contains an identical bulb in series with a capacitor. On closing the switch, which of the following will glow?
optA: Both bulbs will glow at the same time
optB: The bulb with the capacitor will glow faster
optC: The bulb without the capacitor will glow continuously
solution: A capacitor blocks steady direct current. The branch containing it passes a brief charging current, so that bulb flashes momentarily and then goes dark once the capacitor is fully charged. The branch without the capacitor is a complete conducting path, so its bulb draws current continuously and glows steadily. Matches option C.
reviewNote: Figure-dependent, and the printed wording is ambiguous. The paper prints the stem as 'Which of the following will glow quickly?' with option (c) reading 'The bulb without the capacitor will glow faster' — but at the instant of closing, an uncharged capacitor behaves as a short circuit, so both bulbs actually light simultaneously and only the steady behaviour distinguishes them. The stem and option (c) have been reworded to ask about continuous glow, which is the defensible physics. TEACHER TO CONFIRM this rewording before this question is used.

subject: Physics
stem: In a hydroelectric power plant, the energy conversion is—
optC: potential energy of water to electrical energy
solution: Water stored behind a dam holds gravitational potential energy. As it falls this becomes kinetic energy, which spins a turbine, and the coupled generator converts that mechanical energy into electrical energy. The overall conversion is therefore from the potential energy of water to electrical energy. Matches option C.

subject: Physics
stem: Which of the following is a non-conventional source of energy?
solution: Petroleum and coal are fossil fuels and are the classic conventional sources. Nuclear energy from radioactive elements is also classed as conventional in the standard Indian syllabus. Solar energy is renewable and inexhaustible, and is the standard example of a non-conventional source. Matches option D.
reviewNote: Duplicate of an existing bank question (same problem, different option set). Stays PRIVATE.

subject: Physics
stem: In the circuit shown, a 10 V cell drives a network in which a 10 \(\Omega\) resistor in series with a parallel combination of a 5 \(\mu\)F capacitor and a 10 \(\Omega\) resistor forms one branch; a second 10 \(\Omega\) resistor is in parallel with that whole branch; and a further 10 \(\Omega\) resistor is in series with the combination. Net resistance in the circuit is—
solution: In the steady state a capacitor passes no current, so the 5 \(\mu\)F capacitor is an open circuit and the parallel block reduces to its 10 \(\Omega\) resistor alone. The upper branch is then \(10 + 10 = 20\ \Omega\), which in parallel with the lower 10 \(\Omega\) gives \(\frac{20 \times 10}{30} = \frac{20}{3}\ \Omega\). Adding the series 10 \(\Omega\) gives a total of \(\frac{50}{3} \approx 16.67\ \Omega\), and the current is \(I = \frac{10}{50/3} = 0.6\) A. Matches option C.
reviewNote: FLAWED AS PRINTED: the stem asks for the NET RESISTANCE but all four printed options are currents in amperes. The net resistance is 16.67 ohm, which matches no option. Keyed (c) 0.6 A, the current, which is what the option set is actually asking for. Stays PRIVATE. The stem needs repairing before this is used.

subject: Physics
stem: In the circuit shown, a 10 V cell is connected to three resistors of 5 \(\Omega\) each joined in parallel, and this combination is in series with a 10 \(\Omega\) resistor. Find the net resistance.
solution: Three equal resistors in parallel give \(R_p = \frac{R}{3} = \frac{5}{3} \approx 1.67\ \Omega\). This is in series with the 10 \(\Omega\) resistor, so the net resistance is \(10 + \frac{5}{3} = \frac{35}{3} \approx 11.67\ \Omega\). Matches option C.
reviewNote: Figure-dependent: the printed question is a circuit diagram labelled 'Find the net resistance'. The topology has been written into the stem.

subject: Physics
stem: When a stationary bus suddenly begins to move forward, why do passengers tend to fall backward?
solution: The feet of the passengers move forward with the floor of the bus, but the upper body tends to stay where it was because a body at rest resists being set in motion. That resistance is inertia of rest, and it makes the upper body lag behind, so the passenger appears to fall backward. Matches option A.

subject: Physics
stem: If the momentum of an object is doubled, its kinetic energy becomes:
solution: Kinetic energy and momentum are related by \(E = \frac{p^2}{2m}\). At fixed mass the energy is proportional to the square of the momentum, so doubling \(p\) multiplies the energy by \(2^2 = 4\). Matches option A.

subject: Physics
stem: A body is falling freely under gravity in vacuum. Which of the following decreases continuously during the fall?
solution: As the body descends its height falls, so its gravitational potential energy \(mgh\) decreases steadily. That lost potential energy reappears as kinetic energy, which therefore increases, and the speed increases so the momentum increases too. In a vacuum there is no air resistance, so the total mechanical energy stays constant. Matches option A.

subject: Physics
stem: A ball is thrown vertically upward with a speed of 20 m/s. (Take \(g = 10\) m/s\(^2\)) What is the maximum height reached?
solution: At the highest point the velocity is zero, so \(v^2 = u^2 - 2gh\) gives \(0 = 20^2 - 2 \times 10 \times h\), hence \(h = \frac{400}{20} = 20\) m. Matches option A.
reviewNote: FLAWED AS PRINTED: options (a) and (c) are both '20 m', and 20 m is the correct answer, so the question has two correct choices. Keyed the first occurrence, (a). Stays PRIVATE. One of the duplicated options needs replacing before this is used.

subject: Physics
stem: Which of the following is an example of a conservative force?
solution: A conservative force does work that depends only on the endpoints and not on the path taken, so the work around any closed loop is zero and a potential energy can be defined for it. Gravity satisfies this. Friction, air resistance and viscous drag are all dissipative: they oppose motion and convert mechanical energy irreversibly into heat, so the work done depends on the path length. Matches option B.

subject: Physics
stem: Which of the following rays will not be deflected by an electromagnetic field?
solution: Electric and magnetic fields exert forces only on charged particles. Alpha rays are helium nuclei and carry positive charge, beta rays are electrons or positrons, and cathode rays are streams of electrons, so all three are deflected. Gamma rays are high-energy electromagnetic radiation with no charge and no rest mass, so no field deflects them. Matches option C.

subject: Physics
subtopic: Simple Harmonic Motion and General Waves
stem:
Which of the following about waves is/are correct?

1. In longitudinal waves, particles of the medium vibrate parallel to the direction of wave propagation.
2. In transverse waves, particles of the medium vibrate perpendicular to the direction of wave propagation.
3. Sound waves in air are transverse waves.
4. S-waves in earthquakes are transverse waves.
solution: Statement 1 is the definition of a longitudinal wave and is correct. Statement 2 is the definition of a transverse wave and is correct. Statement 3 is wrong: sound in air propagates by compressions and rarefactions, so it is longitudinal, and a gas cannot sustain the shear needed for a transverse wave. Statement 4 is correct, since seismic S-waves are shear waves and are transverse, which is why they cannot travel through the liquid outer core. So 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Matches option D.

subject: Physics
stem: A photon of X-ray has an energy of 5 keV, while a photon of visible light has an energy of 2 eV. Which of the following statements is incorrect?
optA: The wavelength of the X-ray photon is less than that of the visible light photon
optC: The speeds of the photons in vacuum are different
optD: The frequency of the X-ray photon is higher than that of the visible light photon
solution: All electromagnetic radiation travels at the same speed \(c\) in vacuum regardless of its energy, so option C is the incorrect statement and is therefore the answer. The others are all true: 5 keV differs from 2 eV, and since \(E = h\nu = \frac{hc}{\lambda}\), the more energetic X-ray photon has the higher frequency and the shorter wavelength. Matches option C.

subject: Physics
stem: Which one of the following statements about X-rays is not true?
optB: These can be generated by bombarding a metal target with high energy electrons
optC: Due to their wavelengths being shorter, these can be used for radar systems
optD: These are also used for the treatment of certain forms of cancer
solution: Radar operates in the microwave and radio part of the spectrum, at wavelengths of centimetres, not at the angstrom wavelengths of X-rays, so option C is untrue and is the answer. The other three are correct: X-ray wavelengths are of the order of 1 angstrom, they are produced by stopping fast electrons in a metal target, and they are used in radiotherapy. Matches option C.
reviewNote: Exact duplicate of an existing bank question, same stem and same options. Stays PRIVATE.

subject: Physics
stem: \(\gamma\)-rays consist of:
solution: Gamma radiation is emitted when an excited nucleus drops to a lower energy state. It carries no charge and no rest mass and is simply electromagnetic radiation of very short wavelength, at the high-energy end of the spectrum beyond X-rays. Matches option D.

subject: Physics
stem: When a white light beam falls on a hollow prism filled with water, it splits into seven colours. Which colour suffers the maximum angle of deviation?
optD: All suffer equal amount of deviation
solution: The refractive index of a medium increases as the wavelength decreases, and the deviation produced by a prism increases with refractive index. Violet has the shortest wavelength of the seven colours, so it has the largest refractive index and is deviated most; red, with the longest wavelength, is deviated least. Matches option B.

subject: Physics
stem: The blackboard seems black because it—
solution: We see an object by the light it sends to the eye. A surface appears black when it absorbs essentially all the visible wavelengths falling on it and reflects none back. A surface reflecting every colour would appear white, and black is the absence of reflected light rather than a colour that can itself be absorbed or reflected. Matches option B.

subject: Physics
subtopic: Refraction, Speed of Light and TIR
stem: A ray of light passes from air into glass. What happens to the ray?
optA: speeds up and bends away from the normal
optB: speeds up and bends towards the normal
optC: slows down and bends away from the normal
optD: slows down and bends towards the normal
solution: Glass is optically denser than air, so its refractive index is higher and the speed of light in it is lower. A ray entering a denser medium bends towards the normal, which follows from Snell's law \(n_1\sin i = n_2\sin r\): with \(n_2 > n_1\) the angle of refraction is smaller than the angle of incidence. Matches option D.

subject: Physics
stem: The flattening of the Sun and its red colour during sunrise and sunset are due to:
solution: The Sun's disc looks flattened because light from its lower edge travels a longer slanting path through the atmosphere and is refracted more than light from the upper edge, compressing the disc vertically; that is atmospheric refraction. The red colour arises because the long path scatters away the shorter blue wavelengths and leaves the longer red ones, which is scattering. Taking the two effects in the order the question names them, flattening then colour, gives refraction then scattering. Matches option C.
reviewNote: FLAWED AS PRINTED: options (c) and (d) name the SAME two phenomena in reverse order, so both are defensible answers. Keyed (c) because it lists the causes in the same order the stem lists the effects. Stays PRIVATE. One of the two options needs replacing before this is used.

subject: Physics
stem: Which statement is correct about a secondary rainbow?
optA: fainter and formed at a larger angle
solution: A secondary rainbow is produced by two internal reflections inside each raindrop instead of one. The extra reflection loses light, so the bow is fainter, and it appears at about 51 degrees against roughly 42 degrees for the primary, that is at a larger angle. The double reflection also reverses the colour order, but the colours remain separated. Matches option A.

subject: Physics
stem: A plane mirror is 80 cm tall. Which of the following persons cannot see their full image in the mirror?
solution: To see a full-length image in a plane mirror a person needs a mirror of at least half their own height, a result that follows from the laws of reflection and is independent of how far away they stand. An 80 cm mirror therefore serves anyone up to \(2 \times 80 = 160\) cm tall. The person of 170 cm exceeds this and cannot see their full image. Matches option D.

subject: Physics
stem: Viewfinders used in automobiles to locate vehicles behind are made of:
solution: A convex mirror always forms an erect, diminished, virtual image and, because it diverges the reflected light, it covers a much wider field of view than a plane mirror of the same size. That wide field is exactly what a driver needs to watch the traffic behind, which is why rear-view mirrors are convex. Matches option C.

subject: Physics
stem: An object is kept 5 cm in front of a concave mirror of focal length 15 cm. What will be the nature of the image?
solution: The object distance of 5 cm is less than the focal length of 15 cm, so the object lies between the pole and the principal focus. For a concave mirror this is the one position that gives a virtual, erect and enlarged image behind the mirror. Using the mirror formula with \(u = -5\) and \(f = -15\) gives \(v = +7.5\) cm and magnification \(m = -\frac{v}{u} = +1.5\), confirming a virtual image magnified one and a half times. Matches option B.

subject: Physics
stem: Which of the following statements is not true about a plane mirror?
optA: A plane mirror can be considered as a spherical mirror with infinite focal length
optB: The image formed by a plane mirror is virtual and upright
optC: The image formed by a plane mirror is of the same size as the object
optD: The image formed by a plane mirror is real and inverted
solution: A plane mirror always forms a virtual, erect image of the same size as the object, located as far behind the mirror as the object is in front. Option D contradicts this on both counts and is therefore the untrue statement. Option A is a valid limiting description, since a plane surface is a sphere of infinite radius and hence of infinite focal length. Matches option D.

subject: Physics
stem:
Which of the following statements about eye defects is correct?

1. In myopia, the eyeball is too long, and the image of a distant object forms in front of the retina.
2. Myopia is corrected using a concave lens, whose focal length is negative.
3. In hypermetropia, the eyeball is too short, and the image of a nearby object forms behind the retina.
4. Hypermetropia is corrected using a concave lens.
solution: Statement 1 is correct, since an elongated eyeball converges distant light before the retina. Statement 2 is correct, because a diverging concave lens with negative focal length pushes that image back onto the retina. Statement 3 is correct, since a shortened eyeball does not converge light from a near object soon enough. Statement 4 is wrong: hypermetropia needs additional converging power and is corrected with a convex lens. So 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Matches option C.

subject: Physics
subtopic: Simple Harmonic Motion and General Waves
stem:
Which of the following statements are correct?

1. Sound waves in air are longitudinal waves.
2. Light waves are transverse waves.
3. Longitudinal waves have particle motion perpendicular to the direction of wave propagation.
4. Transverse waves have particle motion parallel to the direction of wave propagation.
solution: Statement 1 is correct, since sound in air travels as compressions and rarefactions along the direction of travel. Statement 2 is correct, since light is an electromagnetic wave whose fields oscillate at right angles to the direction of propagation. Statements 3 and 4 invert the two definitions and are both wrong. So only 1 and 2 are correct. Matches option A.
reviewNote: FLAWED AS PRINTED: options (a) and (d) are both '1 and 2 only', which is also the correct answer, so the question has two correct choices. Keyed the first occurrence, (a). Stays PRIVATE.

subject: Physics
subtopic: Sound Behaviours — Reflection, Echo, Reverberation, Beats
stem: A person stands in front of a cliff and claps. He hears the echo after 3 seconds. If the speed of sound in air is 330 m/s, what is the distance between the person and the cliff?
solution: In the 3 seconds before the echo returns, the sound travels to the cliff and back, so the total path is \(330 \times 3 = 990\) m. The distance to the cliff is half of that, \(\frac{990}{2} = 495\) m. Matches option B.

subject: Physics
subtopic: Wave Equation, Speed, and Frequency Bands
stem: The speed of sound is maximum in which of the following?
solution: Sound needs a material medium, so it does not travel in a vacuum at all, ruling out option D. Its speed depends on the elasticity and density of the medium and is greatest where the particles are most tightly coupled. Solids are far more elastic than liquids or gases, so sound is fastest in steel, at roughly 5000 m/s against about 1500 m/s in water and 340 m/s in air. Matches option C.

subject: Physics
stem: An electric heater is rated 1500 watt. If electric power costs \(\text{Rs.}\,2\) per kilowatt-hour, then the cost of power for 10 hours running of the heater is:
solution: The heater draws 1500 W, that is 1.5 kW. Running for 10 hours it consumes \(1.5 \times 10 = 15\) kilowatt-hours. At 2 rupees per unit the cost is \(15 \times 2 = 30\) rupees. Matches option A.

subject: Physics
stem: Seat belts in cars are used to protect passengers because they demonstrate the application of:
solution: In a sudden stop the car decelerates but the passenger, by inertia, continues to move forward at the original speed. That tendency of a body in motion to stay in motion is Newton's first law, and the seat belt supplies the external force needed to stop the passenger with the car. Matches option A.

subject: Physics
stem: A body of mass 2 kg moving at 5 m/s is brought to rest in 0.5 s by a constant force. The magnitude of the force is:
solution: The change in momentum is \(\Delta p = m(v - u) = 2(0 - 5) = -10\) kg m/s. By the impulse-momentum theorem the force is the rate of change of momentum, so \(|F| = \frac{|\Delta p|}{t} = \frac{10}{0.5} = 20\) N. Equivalently \(a = \frac{0-5}{0.5} = -10\) m/s\(^2\) and \(F = ma = 2 \times 10 = 20\) N. Matches option C.
reviewNote: AUTHORED REPLACEMENT. The source document skips Q47 entirely (it runs Q46, Q48), so this question was written to fill the gap and bring the Physics section to 50. It is not from the original paper and needs teacher approval before use.

subject: Physics
stem: The momentum of a body is tripled. Its kinetic energy becomes:
solution: Kinetic energy is related to momentum by \(E = \frac{p^2}{2m}\), so at constant mass the energy varies as the square of the momentum. Tripling \(p\) multiplies the energy by \(3^2 = 9\). Matches option C.

subject: Physics
stem: A good material for a cooking utensil should have:
optA: High heat capacity and low thermal conductivity
optB: Low heat capacity and high thermal conductivity
optC: Low heat capacity and low thermal conductivity
optD: High heat capacity and high thermal conductivity
solution: High thermal conductivity is wanted so that heat passes quickly from the flame through the base to the food. Low heat capacity is wanted so that the vessel itself absorbs little of the heat supplied and warms up rapidly, leaving most of the energy for the food and allowing the temperature to be controlled quickly. Matches option B.

subject: Physics
stem: Which of the following is not a unit of energy?
solution: The joule is the SI unit of energy, the calorie is the heat needed to raise one gram of water by one degree Celsius, and the electronvolt is the energy gained by an electron across one volt; all three measure energy. The dyne is the CGS unit of FORCE, equal to \(10^{-5}\) N, and so is the odd one out. Matches option D.
reviewNote: Duplicate of an existing bank question (same problem, different option set). Stays PRIVATE.

subject: Geography
subtopic: Mountains, Plateaus and Plains of India
stem: Arrange the following mountains in the right sequence from south to north:
solution: Doddabetta is the highest peak of the Nilgiris in Tamil Nadu at about 11 degrees north, so it is the southernmost. The Vindhyanchal range runs across central India at about 23 degrees north. Dhaulagiri lies in the Nepal Himalaya at about 28.7 degrees north, and Mount Kailash is in Tibet at about 31 degrees north, the northernmost of the four. The south-to-north order is therefore Doddabetta, Vindhyanchal, Dhaulagiri, Kailash. Matches option B.

subject: Geography
subtopic: Mountains, Plateaus and Plains of India
stem:
Identify the correct pair:

| Place of pilgrimage | Location |
|---|---|
| 1. Srisailam | Nallamalla hills |
| 2. Omkareshwar | Satmala Hills |
| 3. Pushkar | Mahadeo hills |
solution: Srisailam, the Mallikarjuna Jyotirlinga on the Krishna in Andhra Pradesh, does lie in the Nallamala hills, so pair 1 is correct. Omkareshwar is on an island in the Narmada in Madhya Pradesh, not in the Satmala hills, which are in Maharashtra, so pair 2 is wrong. Pushkar is in Rajasthan and lies in the Aravalli, not the Mahadeo hills of the Satpura in Madhya Pradesh, so pair 3 is wrong. Only pair 1 is correct. Matches option A.

subject: Geography
subtopic: Mountains, Plateaus and Plains of India
stem:
Which among the following peaks are not situated in India?

1. Dhaulagiri
2. Kamet
3. Makalu
4. Nanda Devi
solution: Dhaulagiri lies wholly within Nepal and Makalu stands on the Nepal-China border, so neither is in India. Kamet is in the Garhwal Himalaya of Uttarakhand and Nanda Devi is the second highest peak in India, also in Uttarakhand, so both of those are Indian. The peaks not in India are 1 and 3. Matches option B.

subject: Geography
subtopic: Mountains, Plateaus and Plains of India
stem:
Identify the correct pairs:

| Peak | Mountains |
|---|---|
| 1. Namcha Barwa | Garhwal Himalayas |
| 2. Nanda Devi | Kumaon Himalayas |
| 3. Nokrek | Sikkim Himalayas |
solution: Namcha Barwa marks the eastern extremity of the Himalaya in Tibet, where the Tsangpo turns south, and is nowhere near the Garhwal Himalaya, so pair 1 is wrong. Nanda Devi does stand in the Kumaon Himalaya of Uttarakhand, so pair 2 is correct. Nokrek is the highest point of the Garo Hills in Meghalaya and is not part of the Sikkim Himalaya, so pair 3 is wrong. Only pair 2 is correct. Matches option B.

subject: Geography
subtopic: Mountains, Plateaus and Plains of India
stem:
Identify the correct pairs:

| Hills | Region |
|---|---|
| 1. Cardamom Hills | Coromandel coast |
| 2. Kaimur Hills | Konkan Coast |
| 3. Mahadeo Hills | Central India |
| 4. Mikir Hills | North East India |
solution: The Cardamom Hills are the southern end of the Western Ghats in Kerala and Tamil Nadu, on the Malabar side, not the Coromandel coast, so pair 1 is wrong. The Kaimur Hills are an inland Vindhyan range across Bihar, Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh, far from the Konkan coast, so pair 2 is wrong. The Mahadeo Hills are part of the Satpura in Madhya Pradesh, which is central India, and the Mikir Hills, now the Karbi Anglong plateau, are in Assam in the north-east. Pairs 3 and 4 are correct. Matches option C.

subject: Geography
subtopic: Mountains, Plateaus and Plains of India
stem: Which one of the following is the oldest mountain range in India?
solution: The Aravalli are fold mountains of Precambrian age, formed more than a billion years ago, and are among the oldest ranges on Earth. Long denudation has worn them down to low residual hills. The Himalaya, by contrast, are young fold mountains still rising, and the Satpura and Nilgiri are both younger than the Aravalli. Matches option B.

subject: Geography
subtopic: Mountains, Plateaus and Plains of India
stem: Velikonda Hills, which is a part of the Eastern Ghats, is situated in
solution: The Velikonda range is the easternmost of the parallel ridges of the Eastern Ghats in Andhra Pradesh, running through the Nellore and Prakasam districts roughly parallel to the Coromandel coast. Matches option D.
reviewNote: The printed stem spells the range 'Veliconda'; transcribed as the standard spelling 'Velikonda'.

subject: Geography
subtopic: Mountains, Plateaus and Plains of India
stem:
Identify the correct pairs:

| Peak | State |
|---|---|
| A. Doddabetta | 1. Maharashtra |
| B. Guru Shikhar | 2. Madhya Pradesh |
| C. Kalsubai | 3. Tamil Nadu |
| D. Dhupgarh | 4. Rajasthan |
solution: Doddabetta is the highest peak of the Nilgiris in Tamil Nadu, giving 3. Guru Shikhar is the highest point of the Aravalli, on Mount Abu in Rajasthan, giving 4. Kalsubai is the highest peak in Maharashtra, in the Sahyadri, giving 1. Dhupgarh is the highest point of the Satpura, in the Pachmarhi area of Madhya Pradesh, giving 2. The matching is A-3, B-4, C-1, D-2. Matches option C.

subject: Geography
subtopic: Mountains, Plateaus and Plains of India
stem: The hill range that separates the state of Manipur from the state of Nagaland is known as
solution: The Barail range is the highest of the Assam-Naga hill ranges and runs between the Naga Hills and the Manipur hills, forming the divide between Nagaland and Manipur and separating the Brahmaputra and Barak drainage. The Arakan Yoma lies in Myanmar and the Patkai range forms the boundary with Myanmar in the north-east. Matches option C.

subject: Geography
subtopic: Mountains, Plateaus and Plains of India
stem: Which one among the following statements is not correct?
optA: Shillong Plateau is an outlier of Peninsular Plateau of India
optB: Aravali mountain is the oldest mountain chain in India
optC: Vindhyas are example of fold mountains
optD: Rajmahal Highlands are composed of lava deposits
solution: The Vindhyas are not fold mountains. They are a block or relict range, an escarpment produced by faulting and long denudation of horizontally bedded Vindhyan sediments, so option C is the incorrect statement and is the answer. The other three are correct: the Shillong plateau is a detached north-eastern outlier of the peninsular block, the Aravalli are India's oldest range, and the Rajmahal hills are built of basaltic lava flows of the Rajmahal traps. Matches option C.

subject: Geography
subtopic: Forests and Natural Vegetation of India
stem:
Consider the following:

1. Keoladeo Ghana National Park
2. Mudumalai Wildlife Sanctuary
3. Sultanpur National Park

Which of the above are wetlands?
solution: Keoladeo Ghana at Bharatpur is a man-made freshwater marsh, a Ramsar site and a famous wintering ground for waterfowl. Sultanpur in Haryana is likewise a shallow freshwater lake and a Ramsar site. Mudumalai, on the Nilgiri slopes in Tamil Nadu, is a tropical dry and moist deciduous forest and a tiger reserve, not a wetland. So 1 and 3 are wetlands. Matches option C.

subject: Geography
subtopic: Forests and Natural Vegetation of India
stem: Which of the following national parks is unique in being a swamp with floating vegetation that supports a rich biodiversity?
solution: Keibul Lamjao, on Loktak Lake in Manipur, is the only floating national park in the world. It rests on phumdis, mats of decomposing vegetation and soil that float on the lake, and is the last natural refuge of the sangai or brow-antlered deer. Bhitarkanika is a mangrove system, while Keoladeo and Sultanpur are ordinary freshwater marshes. Matches option B.

subject: Geography
subtopic: Forests and Natural Vegetation of India
stem: At which of the following places is the Marine National Park located?
solution: India's first marine national park was established in the Gulf of Kachchh, off the coast of the Jamnagar district of Gujarat. It protects an archipelago of coral reef islands together with their mangroves and reef fauna. Matches option D.

subject: Geography
subtopic: Forests and Natural Vegetation of India
stem: Which one among the following is the correct order of tiger reserves situated from North to South in India?
solution: Corbett is in Uttarakhand at about 29.5 degrees north, Sariska is in Rajasthan at about 27.3 degrees north, Simlipal is in Odisha at about 22 degrees north, and Periyar is in Kerala at about 9.5 degrees north. Reading from north to south gives Corbett, Sariska, Simlipal, Periyar. Matches option C.
reviewNote: Exact duplicate of an existing bank question, same stem and same options. Stays PRIVATE.

subject: Geography
chapter: Indian Geography — Economy, Resources and Transport
stem:
Which of the following are UNESCO recognised world heritage sites?

1. Caves of Ajanta
2. Temple and caves at Ellora
3. Mandapas of Mahabalipuram
4. Caves of Kanheri
solution: The Ajanta Caves and the Ellora Caves, both in Maharashtra, were inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage list in 1983, and the Group of Monuments at Mahabalipuram in Tamil Nadu, which includes the rock-cut mandapas, was inscribed in 1984. The Kanheri Caves in the Sanjay Gandhi National Park in Mumbai, though an important Buddhist site, are not on the list. So 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Matches option B.

subject: Geography
subtopic: Location, Extent and Frontiers of India
stem: The expression 'South Asia' usually includes
optA: Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan and Sri Lanka
optB: Nepal, Bhutan, India, Afghanistan, China, Pakistan, Sri Lanka
optC: Bangladesh, India, China, Nepal, Japan, Pakistan and Maldives
optD: Bangladesh, Bhutan, China, Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan and Sri Lanka
solution: South Asia is conventionally the Indian subcontinent and its immediate neighbours: Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, the Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan and Sri Lanka, which are also the seven founding members of SAARC. China and Japan are East Asian and are excluded, which rules out options B, C and D. Matches option A.

subject: Geography
subtopic: Location, Extent and Frontiers of India
stem: How many Indian states share their border with Myanmar?
solution: Four Indian states adjoin Myanmar: Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, Manipur and Mizoram. Together they account for a land boundary of roughly 1,643 km. Matches option B.

subject: Geography
subtopic: Location, Extent and Frontiers of India
stem: In India, how many States share the coastline?
solution: Nine states have a sea coast: on the west Gujarat, Maharashtra, Goa, Karnataka and Kerala, and on the east Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Odisha and West Bengal. The union territories with coastlines, such as Puducherry, Daman and Diu, Lakshadweep and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, are not states and are excluded. Matches option C.

subject: Geography
subtopic: Location, Extent and Frontiers of India
stem: Which one among the following creeks is not associated with the state of Gujarat?
solution: Kori Creek is a tidal creek in the Rann of Kachchh, the abandoned mouth of the Indus, and Sir Creek is the disputed 96 km tidal estuary on the Gujarat-Sindh boundary. Both are firmly associated with Gujarat, which also rules out option D. That leaves Kajhar Creek as the one not associated with the state. Matches option C.
reviewNote: Low confidence on the distractor: 'Kajhar Creek' is not a recognised Indian coastal feature under that name, so the key rests on eliminating the two well-known Gujarat creeks rather than on positively identifying it.

subject: Geography
stem: The only Indian state having a common border with Sikkim is:
solution: Sikkim is bounded by Nepal on the west, China on the north and east, and Bhutan on the south-east. Its only Indian neighbour is West Bengal, which adjoins it on the south through the Darjeeling district. Matches option D.

subject: Geography
subtopic: Mountains, Plateaus and Plains of India
stem:
Arrange the following places of Kashmir from north to south:

1. Srinagar
2. Gilgit
3. Kargil
4. Banihal
solution: Gilgit is the northernmost at about 35.9 degrees north, followed by Kargil in Ladakh at about 34.5 degrees, then Srinagar in the Kashmir valley at about 34.1 degrees, and finally Banihal on the southern rim of the valley at about 33.4 degrees. Reading north to south gives 2, 3, 1, 4. Matches option C.

subject: Geography
chapter: Indian Geography — Economy, Resources and Transport
subtopic: Energy and Industries — Power, Petroleum, Iron and Steel
stem: Which one of the following is the oldest Nuclear Power Plant in India?
solution: Tarapur in Maharashtra was India's first nuclear power station, commissioned in 1969 with two boiling water reactors built with American assistance. Kakrapar followed in 1993, Kaiga in 2000 and Kudankulam, the newest of the four, in 2013. Matches option B.
reviewNote: The printed option (c) reads 'Kundankulam'; transcribed as the standard spelling 'Kudankulam'.

subject: Geography
subtopic: Mountains, Plateaus and Plains of India
stem:
Correctly match the mountain passes and the states they are associated with:

| Passes | States |
|---|---|
| A. Zoji La | 1. Himachal Pradesh |
| B. Lipu Lekh | 2. Sikkim |
| C. Shipki La | 3. Uttarakhand |
| D. Nathu La | 4. Jammu and Kashmir |
solution: Zoji La carries the Srinagar-Leh road over the Great Himalaya in the Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh region, giving 4. Lipu Lekh links Uttarakhand with Tibet and is the traditional Kailash-Mansarovar route, giving 3. Shipki La is the pass through which the Sutlej enters India in Himachal Pradesh, giving 1. Nathu La connects Sikkim with the Chumbi valley in Tibet, giving 2. The matching is A-4, B-3, C-1, D-2. Matches option D.

subject: Geography
subtopic: Location, Extent and Frontiers of India
stem: Which one of the following is the correct sequence of the positions in the Bay of Bengal from North to South?
optA: Palk Strait, Gulf of Mannar, Palk Bay
optB: Gulf of Mannar, Palk Strait, Palk Bay
optC: Palk Bay, Palk Strait, Gulf of Mannar
optD: Palk Strait, Palk Bay, Gulf of Mannar
solution: Moving south along the coast between India and Sri Lanka, the Palk Strait comes first at about 10 degrees north, then the Palk Bay, which is the pocket of water enclosed to its south by Rameswaram island and Adam's Bridge, and finally the Gulf of Mannar south of that chain of shoals at about 9 degrees north. The north-to-south order is Palk Strait, Palk Bay, Gulf of Mannar. Matches option D.

subject: Geography
subtopic: Mountains, Plateaus and Plains of India
stem: Where is Aghil Pass located?
solution: The Aghil Pass lies in the Aghil range north of the Karakoram, on the route from Ladakh towards the Yarkand valley in Xinjiang. The Karakoram and Aghil ranges belong to the Trans-Himalayan system, which lies beyond the Great Himalaya. Matches option B.

subject: Geography
stem: Which one among the following is not correct regarding the black soil of Peninsular India?
optA: Rich in iron, lime and potash
optC: Fertile and well suited for growing sugarcane
optD: Rich in phosphorus and organic matter
solution: Black or regur soil, formed from weathered Deccan basalt, is deficient in phosphorus, nitrogen and organic matter, so option D is the incorrect statement and is the answer. The other three are true: it is rich in iron, lime, magnesia and potash, its high clay content makes it highly moisture retentive so that it can be cropped in the dry season, and it supports cotton, sugarcane and other crops. Matches option D.

subject: Geography
chapter: Earth's Structure, Landforms and Geological Time
stem: Soils which reflect the composition of underlying rocks are always
solution: A young or immature soil has had little time for weathering, leaching and horizon development, so its mineral composition still closely mirrors the parent rock beneath it. As a soil matures, climate and vegetation increasingly dominate, horizons develop and the parent material's signature is progressively lost. Matches option A.

subject: Geography
stem:
Which of the following statements regarding laterite soil of India is correct?

1. They are generally red in colour
2. They are rich in nitrogen and potash
3. They are well developed in Rajasthan and UP
4. Tapioca and cashew nuts grow well on these soils
solution: Statement 1 is correct: heavy leaching leaves iron and aluminium oxides behind, giving laterite its red colour. Statement 2 is wrong, since laterite is poor in nitrogen, phosphate, potash and lime. Statement 3 is wrong, because laterite forms under a hot, seasonally very wet climate and occurs on the Western Ghats, the Eastern Ghats, Meghalaya and parts of Kerala, Karnataka and Odisha, not in the dry north-west. Statement 4 is correct, as tapioca and cashew are the characteristic laterite crops of the Malabar coast. So 1 and 4 are correct. Matches option C.

subject: Geography
chapter: Earth's Structure, Landforms and Geological Time
stem: Soil is a complex mixture formed by weathering of rocks and contains variable proportions of silt, clay, sand, humus, microbes and so on. The order of the three main components of soil (sand, silt and clay) as per their particle size is:
optA: silt greater than sand greater than clay
optB: sand greater than silt greater than clay
optC: clay greater than sand greater than silt
optD: clay greater than silt greater than sand
solution: By the standard soil texture classification, sand particles are the coarsest at roughly 0.05 to 2 mm, silt is intermediate at about 0.002 to 0.05 mm, and clay is the finest at under 0.002 mm. In decreasing order of particle size the sequence is sand, then silt, then clay. Matches option B.

subject: Geography
stem: Which one among the following is the coral group of islands of India?
solution: The Lakshadweep group in the Arabian Sea is entirely of coral origin, made up of atolls, reefs and coral banks built on a submerged volcanic ridge. The Andaman and Nicobar islands in the Bay of Bengal are the emergent tops of a submarine mountain range and are tectonic, not coral. Minicoy is a single island within Lakshadweep rather than the group itself, so the group asked for is Lakshadweep. Matches option D.

subject: Geography
subtopic: World — Rivers, Canals and Water Bodies
stem: In deep ponds and lakes, which one of the following vertical zones receives least light penetration?
solution: The profundal zone is the deep water lying below the level to which effective light penetrates, so photosynthesis cannot be sustained there and the zone depends on organic matter sinking from above. The littoral is the shallow, well-lit margin, and the limnetic is the open, sunlit surface water above the compensation depth. Matches option D.

subject: Geography
subtopic: Indian Rivers, Lakes and Water Bodies
stem: Which of the following is an artificial lake?
solution: Kodaikanal Lake is man-made, created in the 1860s by damming a valley in the Palani hills. Kolleru is a natural freshwater lagoon between the Krishna and Godavari deltas, Nainital is a natural tectonic lake in a Kumaon depression, and Renuka is a natural lake in the Sirmaur district. Matches option A.

subject: Geography
subtopic: Indian Rivers, Lakes and Water Bodies
stem:
Which of the following pairs are correctly matched?

1. Chilka Lake : Odisha
2. Kolleru Lake : Kerala
3. Pulicat Lake : Karnataka
solution: Chilika is indeed in Odisha, so pair 1 is correct. Kolleru lies in Andhra Pradesh between the Krishna and Godavari deltas, not in Kerala, so pair 2 is wrong. Pulicat straddles the Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu boundary north of Chennai and has nothing to do with Karnataka, so pair 3 is wrong. Only pair 1 is correct. Matches option A.

subject: Geography
subtopic: Indian Rivers, Lakes and Water Bodies
stem: Which one among the following lakes is situated on the west coast of India?
solution: Ashtamudi is a palm-shaped backwater lagoon in the Kollam district of Kerala, on the Arabian Sea coast, and is a Ramsar site. Chilika in Odisha, Pulicat on the Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu border, and Kolleru in Andhra Pradesh all lie on the eastern seaboard. Matches option B.

subject: Geography
chapter: Earth's Structure, Landforms and Geological Time
stem: Which one of the following statements is correct?
optA: In humid tropical region, humus content is high in soil
optD: In equatorial climate, humus content is high in soil
solution: Bacterial activity is slow at low temperatures, so organic matter decomposes only partially and humus accumulates in cold climates, which makes option C correct. In humid tropical and equatorial climates the high heat and moisture cause rapid decomposition and heavy leaching, so humus content is low, ruling out options A and D. Glacial till is a freshly deposited, unsorted parent material with little horizon development, so option B is also wrong. Matches option C.

subject: Geography
chapter: Indian Geography — Economy, Resources and Transport
stem: On which among the following is National Waterway No. 2 situated?
solution: National Waterway 2 is the Brahmaputra stretch from Sadiya to Dhubri in Assam, a distance of about 891 km, declared in 1988. The Haldia to Prayagraj stretch of the Ganga is National Waterway 1 and the West Coast Canal in Kerala is National Waterway 3. Matches option C.

subject: Geography
subtopic: World — Rivers, Canals and Water Bodies
stem:
Identify the correct statements:

1. The Suez Canal is an important link between developed countries and developing countries
2. It links the Mediterranean Sea and the Red Sea
3. It is not a sea level canal
solution: Statement 1 is correct, since the canal is the main artery carrying trade between industrial Europe and the developing economies of Asia and East Africa. Statement 2 is correct: it runs across the Isthmus of Suez joining the Mediterranean at Port Said to the Red Sea at Suez. Statement 3 is wrong, because the Suez Canal is a sea-level canal with no locks, which is precisely what distinguishes it from the Panama Canal. So 1 and 2 are correct. Matches option A.

subject: Geography
chapter: Indian Geography — Economy, Resources and Transport
stem:
Which of the following statements are correct?

1. Kolkata is the only riverine major port of India.
2. The port of Cochin is located on Willingdon Island.
3. Maharashtra has four major ports
4. Mundra port is India's major port in the private sector
solution: Statement 1 is correct: Kolkata is the country's only major riverine port, lying on the Hooghly about 130 km upstream from the sea. Statement 2 is correct, since the Cochin port is built on Willingdon Island, an artificial island in the Kochi backwaters. Statement 3 is wrong, as Maharashtra has two major ports, Mumbai and Jawaharlal Nehru at Nhava Sheva, not four. Statement 4 is correct, Mundra in Gujarat being the country's largest privately operated port. So 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Matches option D.
reviewNote: The printed statement 2 spells it 'Wellington Island'; transcribed as the correct 'Willingdon Island'. Note also that Mundra is a private port rather than a notified 'Major Port' in the statutory sense, though it is the standard intended answer here.

subject: Geography
chapter: Indian Geography — Economy, Resources and Transport
stem: Which one of the following states has more than 2 major ports?
solution: Tamil Nadu has three major ports: Chennai, Kamarajar at Ennore and V. O. Chidambaranar at Tuticorin. Maharashtra has two, Mumbai and Jawaharlal Nehru; West Bengal has one, Kolkata with its Haldia dock complex; and Odisha has one, Paradip. Matches option D.

subject: Geography
chapter: Indian Geography — Economy, Resources and Transport
stem:
Match the following:

| Railway Zone | Headquarters |
|---|---|
| A. West Central | 1. Jabalpur |
| B. South East Central | 2. Gorakhpur |
| C. East Central | 3. Bilaspur |
| D. North Eastern | 4. Hajipur |
solution: West Central Railway has its headquarters at Jabalpur, giving 1. South East Central Railway is headquartered at Bilaspur, giving 3. East Central Railway is at Hajipur in Bihar, giving 4. North Eastern Railway is at Gorakhpur, giving 2. The matching is A-1, B-3, C-4, D-2. Matches option D.

subject: Geography
chapter: Indian Geography — Economy, Resources and Transport
stem: The headquarters of Metro Railway Zone is located in
solution: Metro Railway, Kolkata is a zone of Indian Railways in its own right, the only metro system to hold that status, and its headquarters are in Kolkata. Matches option C.

subject: Geography
stem: The 2011 census has divided the working population of India into 4 major categories. Which one of the following is NOT one of them?
solution: The 2011 Census classifies workers into four categories: cultivators, agricultural labourers, workers in household industry, and other workers. Domestic workers are not a separate census category and would fall within 'other workers'. Matches option B.

subject: Geography
stem:
The All India Census was:

1. 1st attempted in 1872
2. regularly undertaken since 1881
3. always undertaken as a 5 year exercise

Select the correct option:
solution: Statement 1 is correct: the first census across British India was attempted non-synchronously in 1872 under Lord Mayo. Statement 2 is correct, since the first complete synchronous census was taken in 1881 under Lord Ripon and it has been repeated at regular intervals ever since. Statement 3 is wrong, because the Indian census is decennial, taken every ten years, not every five. So 1 and 2 are correct. Matches option C.
reviewNote: The printed stem labels its three statements a., b., c. while the options refer to them as 1, 2 and 3; transcribed with numeric labels so the stem and options agree.

subject: Geography
stem: Which one of the following is the correct ascending sequence of States in terms of population density as per Census 2011?
optA: Arunachal Pradesh - Sikkim - Mizoram - Himachal Pradesh
optB: Arunachal Pradesh - Mizoram - Sikkim - Himachal Pradesh
optC: Mizoram - Arunachal Pradesh - Himachal Pradesh - Sikkim
optD: Arunachal Pradesh - Himachal Pradesh - Sikkim - Mizoram
solution: The 2011 Census densities in persons per square kilometre are Arunachal Pradesh 17, the lowest of any Indian state, Mizoram 52, Sikkim 86 and Himachal Pradesh 123. Arranged in ascending order that gives Arunachal Pradesh, Mizoram, Sikkim, Himachal Pradesh. Matches option B.

subject: Geography
stem: To obtain full benefits of demographic dividend, what should India do?
solution: The demographic dividend is the growth potential of a large working-age population, and it is realised only if that population is productively employed. Skilling and vocational training convert the raw numbers into employable workers and are therefore the direct route to the dividend. Social security and lower infant mortality are desirable in themselves but do not raise the productivity of those already of working age, and privatising higher education is a financing question rather than a skilling strategy. Matches option A.

subject: Geography
chapter: Earth's Structure, Landforms and Geological Time
stem: The Deccan Trap formation was caused by
solution: The Deccan Traps were formed at the end of the Cretaceous when very fluid basaltic lava welled up through long fissures and spread out in successive horizontal sheets over an enormous area, building the characteristic step-like terraces from which the word 'trap' derives. That is a flood basalt or fissure eruption, not the work of a single central vent as in a shield, composite or caldera volcano. Matches option D.

subject: Geography
subtopic: Location, Extent and Frontiers of India
stem: The Gulf of Mannar is situated along the coast of
solution: The Gulf of Mannar lies between the south-eastern coast of Tamil Nadu and the west coast of Sri Lanka, and its chain of 21 islands forms the Gulf of Mannar Marine Biosphere Reserve. Matches option A.
reviewNote: The printed option (c) reads 'Karantaka'; transcribed as 'Karnataka'.

subject: Geography
stem: Which one of the following is closest to Great Nicobar?
solution: Great Nicobar is the southernmost island of the Nicobar group, and Indira Point at its tip is India's southernmost land. The Indonesian island of Sumatra lies only about 145 km to its south-east across the Six Degree Channel, far nearer than Sri Lanka, Java or Borneo. Matches option A.

subject: Geography
stem: Which of the following Union Territories is smallest in terms of geographical area?
solution: Lakshadweep has a land area of only about 32 square kilometres spread over its scattered coral islands, making it the smallest union territory. Daman and Diu covers about 111 square kilometres, Chandigarh about 114, and Dadra and Nagar Haveli about 491. Matches option D.
reviewNote: The printed option (d) reads 'Lakshaweep'; transcribed as 'Lakshadweep'.

subject: Geography
subtopic: Indian Rivers, Lakes and Water Bodies
stem: In some parts of India, consumption of underground water causes mottled teeth and bone damage. Which one of the following is responsible for this?
solution: Excess fluoride in groundwater causes fluorosis. Dental fluorosis shows as mottling and brown staining of the enamel, while prolonged intake causes skeletal fluorosis with stiffness and deformity of the bones. It is a serious problem in parts of Rajasthan, Gujarat, Andhra Pradesh and Telangana. Matches option A.
reviewNote: The printed option (a) reads 'Fluroide'; transcribed as 'Fluoride'.
